claims.statement: docker/Dockerfile is a multi-stage build whose golang:alpine builder cross-compiles for TARGETOS/TARGETARCH/TARGETVARIANT (mapping TARGETVARIANT to GOARM on arm) and runs `CGO_ENABLED=0 ... make V=1 bin/step`, consistent with the Makefile's CGO-disabled default.

The Docker image's final alpine stage creates a non-root step user (uid/gid 1000 via STEPUID/STEPGID), sets ENV STEP and STEPPATH to /home/step, copies bin/step to /usr/local/bin/step, sets STOPSIGNAL SIGTERM, and defaults to CMD ["/bin/bash"].
docker/Dockerfile.debian is the same multi-stage layout built on golang:trixie with a debian:trixie runtime stage (apt-installed make, git, curl, jq, non-root step user).

GoReleaser's default build compiles ./cmd/step with CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, and ldflags `-w -X main.Version=... -X main.BuildTime=...` into bin/step across a target matrix (darwin, linux, freebsd, windows, arm 5/6/7, mips, ppc64le).
A second GoReleaser build (id nfpm) reuses the default build definition but names the binary step-cli for use in packages.

GoReleaser nfpms builds .deb and .rpm packages (package_name step-cli, bindir /usr/bin, vendor Smallstep Labs, GPG-signed) with postinstall/postremove scripts, embedding debian/copyright at /usr/share/doc/step-cli/copyright and ghost files for /usr/bin/step and the bash completion file.

scripts/postinstall.sh registers the update-alternatives link /usr/bin/step (priority 50, target /usr/bin/step-cli) and writes `step completion bash` output to /usr/share/bash-completion/completions/step on install and upgrade.
scripts/postremove.sh removes the step update-alternatives entry on package removal/disappear.
Release artifacts are checksummed into checksums.txt and signed with cosign sign-blob (sigstore bundles) on all artifacts.
GoReleaser publishers upload the packages to Google Cloud Artifact Registry via scripts/package-upload.sh, and snapshot builds use version template {{.Tag}}-next.
scripts/package-upload.sh copies .deb/.rpm packages to gs://artifacts-outgoing via gcloud storage and deliberately skips armhf6 .deb uploads due to a GCP Artifact Registry conflict.

scripts/package-repo-import.sh imports package versions into GCP Artifact Registry repositories (us-central1 by default, rpms and debs) and uses a /tmp/version-deleted.stamp marker to skip re-importing deleted versions.

The repo's debian/ directory contains only changelog and copyright (no debian/control); the changelog points to the GitHub releases page and copyright declares Apache-2.0, so deb/rpm control metadata is generated by GoReleaser nfpms fields.
GoReleaser blobs publish built step binaries to an S3 bucket (AWS_S3_BUCKET, public-read ACL) as extra_files alongside the archives.
Release notes are templated with dl.smallstep.com artifact links for each platform plus .deb/.rpm packages and a cosign verify-blob verification example.

powershell/install-step.ps1 installs step on Windows by downloading step.exe and uninstall-step.ps1 from https://dl.smallstep.com/s3/cli/s3-windows-installer/ into $env:ProgramW6432\Smallstep Labs, adding that directory to the Machine Path, and setting the ssh-agent service to Automatic and starting it.

cert-renewer@.service is a oneshot root unit (STEPPATH=/etc/step-ca, CERT_LOCATION=/etc/step/certs/%i.crt, KEY_LOCATION=/etc/step/certs/%i.key) that runs `step certificate needs-renewal` as ExecCondition and `step ca renew --force` as ExecStart, then ExecStartPost tries `systemctl try-reload-or-restart %i`; it is PartOf=cert-renewer.target.
cert-renewer@.timer fires OnCalendar=*:1/15 (every 15 minutes) with Persistent=true, AccuracySec=1us, and RandomizedDelaySec=5m jitter, WantedBy=timers.target.

ssh-cert-renewer.service is a oneshot root unit (STEPPATH=/etc/step) that renews the Ed25519 SSH host certificate: ExecCondition `step ssh needs-renewal` on /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub, ExecStart `step ssh renew --force`, and ExecStartPost reloads/restarts sshd.service.
ssh-cert-renewer.timer uses the same 15-minute OnCalendar schedule with Persistent=true, AccuracySec=1us, and RandomizedDelaySec=5m.
cert-renewer.target is a systemd target described as restarting all certificate renewers.

systemd/README.md points to the Smallstep "Automating Certificate Renewal" docs and notes the unit files are redirect targets in the files.smallstep.com S3 bucket, so relocating them requires updating the bucket redirects.

step fileserver is a hidden, experimental command that starts an HTTP(S) server serving a directory, with flags --address (default :0), --cert, --key, --roots, and --pidfile; --roots requires both --cert and --key.

With --cert/--key the fileserver serves HTTPS with TLS min version 1.2 and a tlsRenewer providing GetConfigForClient; --roots enables tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert; SIGHUP reloads the certificate, key, and roots, and SIGINT/SIGTERM trigger a 5-second graceful http.Server.Shutdown; the server sets ReadHeaderTimeout 15s.
The fileserver command is enabled by the blank import _ "github.com/smallstep/cli/command/fileserver" in internal/cmd/root.go.

step completion <shell> prints embedded bash, zsh, and fish completion scripts, while the top-level autocomplete/ folder (bash_autocomplete, zsh_autocomplete) is deprecated in favor of `step completion`.

The integration test harness runs in-process: integration/shared_test.go TestMain registers the CLI as a testscript command "step" mapped to internal/cmd's cmd.Run via testscript.Main, so tests do not require a separately built binary.
integration/main_test.go script-tests `step version` (expecting Smallstep CLI/0000000-dev) and that a bogus command fails with a help error.
integration/certificate_test.go generates CSRs and test CAs with keyutil/minica/pemutil and script-tests `step certificate sign` (valid and bad-CSR cases) and `verify` (valid and bad-PEM cases).

integration/certificate_test.go also script-tests `step certificate fingerprint` against testdata/intermediate_ca.crt and defines a custom check_certificate testscript command that parses a certificate bundle from the previous command's stdout.
integration/crypto_test.go script-tests the crypto group: JWK commands (inspect and create RSA/EC/OKP/Oct), JWT, key pair, OTP, and help.

integration/help_test.go checks root --help output and a help-quality report by unmarshaling a usage.Report and asserting headline consistency, per-section word/line thresholds, and absence of TODO strings.

The external release infrastructure referenced by the config (AWS S3 blob bucket, dl.smallstep.com CDN, GCP Artifact Registry, cosign signing identity) lives outside the repository, so its runtime behavior is not verifiable from this codebase.

# Step CLI

`step` is an easy-to-use CLI tool for building, operating, and automating Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) systems and workflows.
It's also a client for the [`step-ca` online Certificate Authority (CA)](https://github.com/smallstep/certificates) server.
You can use it for many common crypto and X.509 operations—either independently, or with an online CA.

**Questions? Ask us on [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/smallstep/certificates/discussions) or [Discord](https://u.step.sm/discord).**

[Contributor's Guide](./docs/CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Features

Step CLI's command groups illustrate its wide-ranging uses:

input.content:
# Quickstart

Practical start for the Smallstep CLI: building the `step` binary, verifying it, bootstrapping against a CA, issuing your first certificate and SSH certificate, and running the tests.

> **What `step` is:** a CLI toolkit for building, operating, and automating PKI workflows, and a client for the separate `step-ca` online CA server ([smallstep/certificates](https://github.com/smallstep/certificates)). CA server behavior (endpoints, provisioning, ACME) is owned by that server; this repository contains the client side.

## Prerequisites and build

- Go — `go.mod` declares `go 1.25.8`; `docs/local-development.md` says the latest two Go versions are supported.
- `make` available on PATH.

```console
$ make bootstrap   # once: installs golangci-lint, gotestsum, govulncheck, goimports, GoReleaser Pro
$ make build       # CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -> bin/step
$ bin/step version
```

`make build` compiles `github.com/smallstep/cli/cmd/step` into `bin/step` with `CGO_ENABLED=0`; `main.Version` and `main.BuildTime` are injected by ldflags (git tag via `GITHUB_REF` or `git describe` in CI, otherwise `-dev`-suffixed). `step version` prints the injected version in `Smallstep CLI/<version>` form.

## Shell completion

`step completion <shell>` prints completion scripts for `bash`, `zsh`, or `fish` (e.g. `step completion bash >> ~/.bashrc`). The checked-in `autocomplete/` scripts are deprecated in favor of this command.

## First CA bootstrap

Point the client at a CA and pin its root:

```console
$ step ca bootstrap --ca-url https://ca.example.com \
    --fingerprint d9d0978692f1c7cc791f5c343ce98771900721405e834cd27b9502cc719f5097
```

`step ca bootstrap` stores the root certificate in `$STEPPATH/certs/root_ca.crt` and creates `$STEPPATH/configs/defaults.json` with the CA url, root certificate location, and fingerprint. `--ca-url` and `--fingerprint` are required (or use the `--team` variant for smallstep.com team CAs, which is incompatible with `--ca-url`/`--fingerprint`). Add `--install` to also install the root into the system trust store.

## First certificate

Generate a one-time token (OTT) on the CA side (e.g. with `step-ca` admin tooling or `step ca token <subject> --provisioner ...` against a CA that allows it), then request a certificate:

```console
$ step ca certificate user@example.com user.crt user.key \
    --token <ott> --san user@example.com
```

`step ca certificate <subject> <crt-file> <key-file>` generates a new private key and a certificate signed by the CA, with flags for `--token`, `--san`, `--issuer`, key type (`--kty`/`--curve`/`--size`), ACME (`--acme`, `--standalone`, `--webroot`), and CA selection (`--ca-url`, `--root`, `--context`).

**Offline mode:** `step ca certificate --offline --ca-config ca.json <subject> <crt> <key>` embeds a CA from a local configuration file (built with `step ca init --ssh --offline`) and signs locally using the `smallstep/certificates` `OfflineCA` library — no CA server required. `--offline` is incompatible with `--token`.

## SSH login

```console
$ step ssh login          # add an SSH user certificate to the local auth agent
$ step ssh config         # write SSH client config (templates from step-certificates)
$ step ssh config --host  # configure an SSH server instead
```

`step ssh login [<identity>]` requests an SSH certificate from the CA and adds it to the authentication agent; `step ssh config` configures OpenSSH to use certificates (`--roots`/`--federation` print verification keys, `--set key=value` customizes templates).

## Running the tests

```console
$ make build && make test    # gotestsum, -short, all packages
$ make lint                  # shared golangci-lint config + govulncheck
```

The `integration/` package uses `testscript` and runs the CLI in-process (the `step` script command maps to `internal/cmd.Run`), so `make test` does not require the binary on PATH. See the development guide for adding tests.

## Uncertainties

- Which CA URL/root is used when `--ca-url`/`--root` are omitted is resolved by the step context machinery in `cli-utils` (external to this repo); the default context values are not defined here.
- The `--team` smallstep.com team CA flow and its endpoints are external; only the flag wiring in this repo is verifiable.
- `step-ca` server-side behavior (provisioners, ACME flows, token issuance) belongs to `smallstep/certificates` and is documented by that project.

claims.statement: step is a CLI toolkit for building, operating, and automating PKI systems and workflows, and a client for the separate step-ca online CA server (smallstep/certificates).
go.mod declares go 1.25.8 and docs/local-development.md requires Go (the latest two versions are supported per the Go support timeline), make, and the repo checked out in $GOPATH.

make bootstrap installs the development toolchain (golangci-lint, gotestsum, govulncheck, goimports, GoReleaser Pro) and is needed only once; make build compiles the CLI into bin/step with CGO_ENABLED=0.

main.Version and main.BuildTime are var placeholders set by LDFLAG at build time, populated by the Makefile ldflags (-X main.Version=$(VERSION) -X main.BuildTime=$(DATE)) from GITHUB_REF or git describe; step version prints the injected version in Smallstep CLI/<version> form.
step completion <shell> prints embedded completion scripts for bash, zsh, and fish; the checked-in autocomplete/ folder scripts are deprecated in favor of this command.

step ca bootstrap --ca-url <uri> --fingerprint <fp> stores the root certificate in $STEPPATH/certs/root_ca.crt and creates $STEPPATH/configs/defaults.json with the CA url, root certificate location, and fingerprint.

The bootstrap action requires --ca-url and --fingerprint together, or the mutually incompatible --team (with optional --team-authority) smallstep.com team variant, and supports --install to install the root certificate.
step ca token <subject> generates an OTT (one-time token) granting access to the CA, used to authenticate certificate requests.

step ca certificate <subject> <crt-file> <key-file> generates a new private key and a certificate signed by the CA, with flags for --token, --san, --issuer, key type, ACME, and CA selection (--ca-url, --root, --context).

Offline mode (step ca certificate --offline --ca-config <file>) embeds a CA from a local configuration and signs without a CA server; --offline is incompatible with --token because the token is generated before the offline CA starts.

The ca-url flag is validated in this repo: an empty value is required-flag unless --offline, an https scheme is enforced (prepended when missing), and IPv6 hosts without brackets are normalized by flags.ParseCaURL/parseCaURL.
step ssh login [<identity>] requests an SSH certificate from the CA and adds it to the local authentication agent.

step ssh config configures OpenSSH to use certificates from templates defined in step-certificates, with --host for server configuration, --roots/--federation to print verification keys, and --set key=value template variables.

make test runs gotestsum over all packages with -short and the integration package runs the CLI in-process via testscript (the step script command maps to internal/cmd.Run), so no separately built binary is required; make lint runs the shared golangci-lint config plus govulncheck.

When --ca-url/--root are omitted, the CA is resolved from the current step context by cautils and cli-utils (external to this repo), so the default context values and context precedence are not established in this codebase.
